text: 🔥🇲🇽 "It was shown that they formed a mafia inside the electoral institutions." "Ballot boxes, voting booths and other things used in the election (...) there was no reason for them to be tied to a single company or two companies." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 12, 2026 Asked what profile the next head of the INE needs, Sheinbaum said that's for the Chamber of Deputies to decide. But the group of companies, the "monopoly, duopoly" that supplied electoral materials, should no longer take part in coming elections; most of them already have their accounts frozen. She welcomed the new contracting guidelines approved by the INE General Council to open competition wherever possible, while keeping security standards for ballots. "These businesses, under different INE and state electoral body leaderships, must be cleaned up. Elections will probably even come out cheaper."

🇲🇽🌎 "One country's development cannot come at the expense of another country's development. It must always be cooperation for development." "With China we don't have a free trade agreement, nor are we heading there, but there is a very important trade relationship with China." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 12, 2026 Sheinbaum will attend the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, November 17–19. She will be a keynote speaker before APEC's Business Advisory Council, more than 1,000 business leaders from 21 economies, on Plan México, and will hold a bilateral meeting with Xi Jinping. Mexico wants to work with China on smart hospitals, waste transformation, science and technology, and renewable energy: "Many solar panels are made in China; they are not made anywhere else in the world, or not at competitive prices." APEC economies account for about 60% of world GDP and 50% of global trade. Mexico was chosen unanimously to host APEC in 2028.
banner: APEC: COOPERATION, NOT AT OTHERS' EXPENSE

text: 🚨🇲🇽 "Since President Trump took office, not a single migrant caravan has reached the northern border." "The vast majority return to their countries of origin once they learn that they are not going to be able to cross." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 12, 2026 On Thursday morning Trump posted a new message about migrant caravans heading to the US and warned that if Mexico doesn't stop them, tariffs would rise 50%. Sheinbaum said there are two caravans right now: one in Arriaga, Chiapas, which formed with about 500 to 600 people and now has fewer than 100, and another that set out from Honduras. Both get humanitarian aid and treatment based on human rights. People who want to go home are helped to return safely; some can stay in Mexico under certain conditions. Asked whether there would be repression: "No, no." The National Migration Institute and the National Guard act "not as an act of repression or violence, but of accompaniment."

🇲🇽🌎 "She was threatened, and for that reason she was given asylum." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 12, 2026 Nadia Beller, a lawyer and the ex-partner of far-right digital strategist Fernando Cerimedo, is now in Mexico after Mexico's embassy in La Paz, Bolivia, granted her asylum and she received safe passage. Cerimedo is jailed in Bolivia, accused of attempted femicide against her. Sheinbaum said Beller has denounced not only the attack but also her ex-partner's involvement in elections in several countries and in social media campaigns against progressive and humanist governments in Latin America. Beller will meet with the Foreign Ministry to decide whether she stays in Mexico or travels on to another country.

🇲🇽🏭 "This new investment helps growth, because we don't import that equipment. It is produced in Mexico." "The investment we are making in transmission and distribution is historic, between two and three times what was invested in previous administrations." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 12, 2026 Brazil's WEG announced a $250 million investment in Mexico through 2030: a new plant in Hidalgo making generators, alternators and transformers for the power grid and data centers, with 2,000 direct jobs and an estimated 4,000 indirect ones. WEG already has more than 6,000 workers in Mexico after about 25 years in the country. Its vice president Daniel Godinho said it makes 100% of the equipment it produces for Mexico here. Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard said foreign direct investment is at historic highs. INEGI data also showed the economy grew 3.2% in the third quarter of 2026 compared with a year earlier, with all three sectors growing.

🇲🇽✊ "A woman reaching the presidency has to do with the struggle of women. It is not an individual effort." "That's why when I took office I said: 'I do not arrive alone, all of us women arrive at the presidency.'" — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 12, 2026 French journalist and former France national team footballer Laure Boulleau asked whether the first woman president had changed mentalities. Sheinbaum said a woman in the presidency is a symbol, and more changes are needed than the symbol, but it is a major cultural change: girls can see they can be whatever they want to be, and boys grow up with a vision of equality. As a girl, she said, she dreamed of being like her mother, a university researcher, and she was a full-time UNAM researcher for about 20 years. Asked how she broke barriers: "Don't give up, always fight, and keep in mind that it is not an individual matter but a collective one."

🇲🇽🌎 "Mexico is a friend of every country in the world." "We work with the United States and have a free trade agreement with them. With China we don't have a free trade agreement, but we still have a trade relationship with them that is important to talk about." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 12, 2026 La Jornada asked how to keep the China trip from being used to obstruct the trade deal being negotiated with the US, after Trump's tariff threat. Sheinbaum noted APEC is an international forum where the US, Mexico, China and Russia all take part. Trump is expected in Shenzhen, but she won't meet him there; a meeting could happen in the US, at Mar-a-Lago, where the G20 will be held. On Mexico's trade deficit with China, she pointed to Plan México, "produce more in Mexico and import less," and the tariffs Mexico raised in December 2025 on certain sectors from countries with no free trade agreement.
banner: "A FRIEND OF EVERY COUNTRY IN THE WORLD"

text:
🇲🇽🏭 <u>Brazil's WEG to invest 50 million in Hidalgo: 2,000 direct jobs</u>

Brazilian electrical-equipment maker WEG will invest 50 million in Hidalgo between 2027 and 2030 to build transformers, generators and alternators for Mexican industry and data centers. The project is expected to create 2,000 direct and 4,000 indirect jobs, taking WEG's Mexican workforce from 6,000 to 8,000. It's another Plan México investment from the Global South, announced days before Sheinbaum flies to APEC. (El Economista)

🇲🇽💳 <u>Banco del Bienestar launches a free, no-fee payments app</u>

The state-owned Banco del Bienestar presented its new mobile app at the mañanera. It lets users send transfers by card number, CLABE account or phone number, and pay or charge by QR code, all without commissions. It also shows balances and transactions instantly and finds the nearest branch. It serves the network that already reaches millions of social-program recipients, and the government made clear that cash will not be eliminated or banned.

🇲🇽🌳 <u>A reserve "created by the people, for the people": Semarnat wants to copy the Sierra Gorda model</u>

In Querétaro's Sierra Gorda Biosphere Reserve, companies pay communities to keep forests standing. Through the Carbono Biodiverso program, ejidos remove cattle, let the forest regrow, and use the money for patrols against illegal logging, road upkeep and local jobs. In 2025 it covered more than 40,000 hectares and 400 landholders and brought in 52 million pesos a year. Environment Secretary Alicia Bárcena toured the reserve and wants the model documented so it can be repeated elsewhere in Mexico.
